chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Asbat, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said:
The one who wants his supplication to be answered, let him purify his earnings.
ai.seo_question: How does the purity of one's earnings affect the acceptance of supplication in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes a causal link between the spiritual efficacy of supplication and the material purity of one's earnings, emphasizing that 'halal' income is a prerequisite for divine acceptance. This teaching reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on the integration of worldly conduct with spiritual devotion, where financial integrity serves as a vessel for spiritual receptivity. The concept underscores that impurity in livelihood creates a barrier between the supplicant and the Divine, a principle deeply rooted in both Quranic exegesis and juristic discussions on trade and consumption.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ali Bin Asbat, from the one who mentioned it, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The one who wants his supplication be Answered for him, so let him purify his earnings’.
en.sarwar: 9. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ali ibn Asbat from those whom he has mentioned (in his book) from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) has said, ‘
Whoever of you wants his prayer answered must make his earning clean.’”
